Training was long, often painful, and at times, I questioned if I was capable of finishing. But with every run, I learned to push through discomfort, to believe in myself, and to run not for others, but for myself.  

On race day, I was nervous, but also excited. The first 10 miles were easy, the miles were steady. But as the miles grew, so did the challenge. My legs were heavy, my mind was tired, and I wanted to stop. But I kept going.  

At 26.5, I was emotional. I was tired. I was proud. I was so proud of myself.  

Finishing was not about the time, but about the effort. It was about the belief that I could do it. It was about knowing that I had trained for it, and, and, I had done it.
